reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E2 shows that rapid heating/cooling (flash Joule heating) successfully produces uniform, homogeneous HEA nanoparticles without segregation, directly contradicting the premise that such conditions inherently limit diffusion and cause phase separation. E3 uses a similar rapid heating step to form disordered solid-solution nanoparticles, again contradicting the claimed baseline. E1 discusses limited mobility in a different, moderate-temperature solid-precursor synthesis, not rapid heating/cooling, and does not address the proposed intervention
premises: Rapid heating/cooling limits atomic diffusion, causing segregation
Extending atomic mixing time (e.g., isothermal hold) enhances diffusion
Enhanced diffusion promotes homogeneous nucleation and single-phase formation
Graded precursor decomposition can delay atomic release and improve mixing
